note: The Democrat of 1835-07-22, Vol. II No. 14, read through. A complete four-page scan, read from the committed derived text (`text/chicago_democrat_1835_07_22.txt`), which resolves on `dev`, so every quote here is machine-checked on this branch. THE TRANSCRIPTION'S GRAIN IS NOT ONE LINE PER PRINTED LINE: the docx rebuild delivers whole half-columns as single lines of up to 5,952 characters, so the claims on page 3 column 4 are cut with `locator.spans` — the character-level citation T-0261 added for the American — and the rest are whole short lines. The advertising of this issue is largely the advertising of 1835-07-08 standing on, which is why several claims here record a WINDOW rather than a new fact; the new matter is the dissolution of Wm. Hogue & Co. (c007, ruling 3's only veto in the four issues T-0296 reads), the Juliet letter list (c010) and Montgomery's Auction Room named and placed on South Water Street (c011). NO CHICAGO POST-OFFICE LETTER LIST: swept for every form the Democrat uses, for one hit, the Juliet return of 1 July 1835.
